retrieved_contexts: Anemia means the blood has a lower than expected capacity to carry oxygen, often reflected by low hemoglobin. Symptoms can include fatigue, weakness, shortness of breath, dizziness, or palpitations. Common evaluation includes complete blood count, iron studies, ferritin, vitamin B12, folate, kidney function, and assessment for blood loss when clinically appropriate.

Pneumonia is an infection or inflammation of the lung tissue. Common symptoms include cough, fever, shortness of breath, fatigue, and chest discomfort. Evaluation may include vital signs, physical examination, pulse oximetry, chest imaging, and selected laboratory tests. Treatment depends on severity, risk factors, likely organism, allergies, and local clinical guidance.

Chest pain can come from cardiac, lung, gastrointestinal, muscle, anxiety-related, or other causes. Potentially serious causes are assessed using symptoms, risk factors, ECG, cardiac biomarkers such as troponin, vital signs, and imaging when needed. Severe, persistent, or concerning chest pain requires urgent clinical assessment.
